name: Circuit training

image.caption: Circuit training by Abersoch beach huts - geograph.org.uk - 7733807

lead: Circuit training moves you through a series of exercise stations with short rests, mixing resistance work and cardio. People use it to lose weight and build conditioning in a short session, which supports a leaner look.

A 2019 meta-analysis of nine randomized trials (837 adults) found circuit training reduced body weight by about 3.8 kg and BMI by 1.8, with the effect significant in participants with overweight or obesity.

paras: A circuit is one pass through a set list of exercises such as push-ups, squat jumps, step-ups or burpees, repeated with brief rests. It can be done with bodyweight or weights.
Typical risks are those of vigorous exercise, such as muscle strain; people with medical conditions are generally advised to consult a clinician first.

social.title: High-Intensity Circuit Training Using Body Weight

chain: Fast rotation of stations with short rests
Lower body weight and fitter physique
angle.text: Circuits raise training volume and heart rate in short sessions, which people use to lose weight and improve fitness; the physique change comes through reduced body fat and increased muscular endurance.

lead: Circuit training is a format developed in 1953 at the University of Leeds by R.E. Morgan and G.T. Anderson, in which exercises are done in a cycle with short rest between stations [1]. It combines endurance training, resistance training and high-intensity aerobics, similar to HIIT [1].

People use it to improve conditioning and body composition within short workouts. A 2019 meta-analysis of nine randomized trials found significant reductions in body weight (-3.81 kg) and BMI (-1.77), significant in overweight and obese groups [2].

paras: One circuit is one pass through all exercises, after which the first is repeated; rests are traditionally short [1]. Typical stations cover upper body (push-ups, bench dips), core (sit-ups), lower body (squat jumps, step-ups) and total body (burpees, jogging) [1].

The Leeds-origin format is described by studies at Baylor University and the Cooper Institute as a time-efficient way to enhance cardiovascular fitness and muscle endurance [1]. The 2019 meta-analysis found weight loss effects in adults [2].

A systematic review and meta-analysis of nine randomized controlled trials in adults found significant decreases in body weight and BMI; subgroup effects were significant for overweight and obese participants [2].
